content:
The atmosphere around Meta AI glasses hasn't been too good lately. It's so serious that today, among the top three paid iPhone apps in the United States, one is specifically designed to detect who nearby might be wearing smart glasses.

The app's name is anything but subtle: Antizuck Smart Glasses Scanner (Anti-Zuckerberg Smart Glasses Scanner). It claims to be able to detect when someone nearby is wearing Meta AI glasses and alert you.

Enough iPhone users are willing to spend $3 to try this app that it currently ranks 3rd on the US iPhone paid App Store charts. New paid apps rarely manage to break into these rankings.

We haven't tested this app and can't confirm whether it really works. Even if it does, what to do after detecting someone wearing AI glasses remains an unknown.

Smart glasses equipped with cameras are actually still quite easy to spot right now, so you probably don't need an app to notice who's wearing them.

However, everyone's attitude is clear. Enough people are fed up with the concept of AI smart glasses, feeling that the matter involves privacy concerns. If Apple wants to enter the smart glasses market next year, this will be a considerable obstacle.
